cards.text: Joshua, Israel's leader, gathers all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. The elders, leaders, judges and officers come too, and they present themselves before God. Then Joshua tells all the people he has a message from the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: The LORD starts way back. Long ago, Israel's fathers lived beyond the Euphrates, including Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor. Back there, they worshiped only the LORD.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "But I took your father Abraham from beyond the Euphrates and led him through all the land of Canaan, and I multiplied his descendants." Picked up out of the back of nowhere and given a whole new life? Baker, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer. I LOVE this part.

cards.question: Abraham's family is about to start growing. Who does the LORD give Abraham?
To Isaac, the LORD gave ___ and Esau. Esau got Mount Seir, but his brother and his sons went down to ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD sends Moses and Aaron, afflicts the Egyptians, and brings Israel out. But at the Red Sea, here come the Egyptians behind them with chariots and horsemen.

cards.question: Water in front of them. Chariots behind them. Friend, that's not a rock and a hard place, that's a sea and a cavalry. What do Israel's fathers do?

answers.text: They cry out to the LORD

cards.question: Israel cries out, and the LORD steps in. What does He put between Israel and the Egyptians?

cards.text: The LORD brings the sea over the Egyptians and engulfs them, and Israel's very eyes saw it. Then Israel lives in the wilderness for a long time, and baker, I did my own long time in a junk drawer, so trust me, that's LONG.

Later the LORD brings them to the Amorites beyond the Jordan, and when the Amorites fight, He delivers them into Israel's hand. Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sets out to fight Israel, and he sends for a man named Balaam son of Beor.

cards.question: Balak, king of Moab, sends for Balaam. What does Balak want Balaam to do to Israel?
The LORD listens to Balaam, so Balaam curses Israel.

cards.text: Balak wanted a curse, and Balaam blesses Israel again and again. AGAIN and AGAIN, Balak! Then Israel crosses the Jordan and comes to Jericho, and Jericho fights them, along with the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites and more.

cards.question: Jericho and a whole list of nations fight Israel. How does it end?

answers.text: The LORD delivers them into Israel's hand
Israel makes a peace treaty with them
Israel retreats back across the Jordan

cards.question: The LORD says Israel drove out the two Amorite kings by their own sword and bow.

cards.text: The LORD sent the hornet ahead of them, and He gave them cities they didn't build and vineyards and olive groves they didn't plant. That's walking into a kitchen where the oven's hot, the dough's mixed and the cookies are already stamped.

cards.question: That's the end of the LORD's words. Now Joshua tells the people to fear the LORD and serve Him in sincerity and truth. What does he tell them to cast aside?

cards.text: Then Joshua says if serving the LORD seems unpleasing to them, "choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve." The gods their fathers served beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites whose land they're living in.

cards.question: Joshua has laid out the choice for all Israel. Then he tells them where he and his house stand. What does he say?

cards.text: The people answer Joshua, "Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods!" That's the whole group chat replying at once.

cards.question: Then the people give their reasons for sticking with the LORD. What do they say He did for them?

answers.text: Gave them a king to lead

cards.text: They finish strong: "We too will serve the LORD, because He is our God!" And then Joshua says something I bet nobody in that crowd expects.

cards.question: The people have just promised to serve the LORD. What does Joshua tell them?

answers.text: You are not able to serve the LORD
The LORD is pleased with you today
You must first build Him an altar

cards.question: Joshua tells the people they're not able to serve the LORD. Why does he say that?

answers.text: He is a holy and jealous God
They are too few to serve Him

cards.text: And Joshua warns them: if they forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, He will turn and bring disaster on them, even after He has been good to them.

cards.question: Joshua just told the people they can't do it. How do they answer him?

answers.text: They insist they will serve the LORD
They ask for more time to decide
They go quiet and head home

cards.text: The people fire back, "No!" Then, "We will serve the LORD!" Joshua says you can't, and they say WATCH US.

cards.question: Joshua points out that the people heard themselves choose to serve the LORD. What does he say they are against themselves?
When Joshua calls them witnesses against themselves, the people refuse to agree.

cards.text: So Joshua says, "get rid of the foreign gods among you and incline your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel." Among you. That's like me swearing I'm off the cookie dough with dough still stuck in my mustache.

cards.question: Joshua tells them to get rid of the foreign gods and turn their hearts to the LORD. What do the people say to Joshua this time?

answers.text: They will serve the LORD and obey His voice
They will think it over until morning
They will decide once each tribe meets

cards.text: On that day Joshua makes a covenant for the people, and there at Shechem he sets a statute and ordinance for them. Then he records these things in the Book of the Law of God.

cards.question: Next Joshua sets something up under the oak near the sanctuary of the LORD. What is it?
Joshua says the large stone under the oak will be a witness against the people. Why?

answers.text: It has heard all the LORD's words to them
It was carried up from the Jordan
Moses carved the Law into it

cards.text: A rock that heard every single word, and it doesn't even have ears. Then Joshua sends the people away, each to his own inheritance.
Some time later, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, dies. They bury him in his own inheritance, at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim.

cards.question: Joshua, the servant of the LORD, dies at the age of ___.
Joshua is gone, but what about that promise at Shechem? Israel served the LORD all through the days of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him.

cards.text: The bones of Joseph, son of Jacob, brought all the way up out of Egypt, are buried at Shechem in the land Jacob bought for a hundred pieces of silver. And Eleazar son of Aaron dies too, and they bury him at Gibeah, which had been given to his son Phinehas.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 18 quotes "choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The included sermon Joshua 24:2-15 doesn't have a stop of its own covering exactly those verses.

rule.text: An included parable or sermon (see passages.md) gets a stop of its own.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop's choice cards by a wide margin: 7 multiple choice (cards 4, 7, 8, 11, 14, 17, 19), 3 true or false (2, 12, 15) and 1 fill in the blank (5).

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop's choice cards by a wide margin: 8 multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12, 14, 15), 2 true or false (10, 19) and 1 fill in the blank (18). The mix also nearly repeats stop 1's pattern.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'A wall of fire' is close to the Exodus account, where the pillar of cloud and fire came between the camps (Exodus 14:19-20, 24). A baker who knows that account could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The setup line 'Joshua says something I bet nobody in that crowd expects' tells the baker the answer on card 4 is a surprise. That rules out the expected wrong answer 'The LORD is pleased with you today'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No card tells the rest of Joshua's warning in Joshua 24:19-20. Cards 5 and 6 leave out 'He will not forgive your rebellion or your sins' and that He will consume them. These are key parts of why Joshua says they are not able to serve the LORD.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card only retells Joshua 24:21, which choice card 7 just covered ('They insist they will serve the LORD'). It is a recap and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'A rock that heard every single word, and it doesn't even have ears' pokes fun at what the text itself says about the stone (Joshua 24:27), so the humor targets Scripture's claim.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.
